subject: Stability signal: Heliotrope latency + errors — ops-cabinet readout
messages:
From: Jordan Silva <j.silva@heliotropehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: service degradation — Heliotrope production

Michael —

We're seeing stora ge-wide latency spikes and a sharp increase in 5xx error rates from your hosted inference endpoint (model: rwd-6b-v2) starting ~08:45 PDT. Throughput dropped intermittently and our checkout flows are timing out for ~30% of requests. Our SRE team is paged; we need confirmation this is on your side and an ETA for remediation.

Quick facts from our side:
- Region: us-west-2
- Affects: Production inference endpoints tied to account HELIO-42 (checkout + receipt generation)
- First observed: 08:45 PDT
- Current symptom: token-level latency up to 2.6s, 500s increasing to 18% of calls

We're happy to jump on a bridge. Please advise next steps and what you need from us.

— Jordan Silva
Director, Platform Engineering
Heliotrope Health

Attachment: heliotrope_sla_alert_0814.txt (stub)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:12:30 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: service degradation — Heliotrope production — ops-cabinet activation

Team —

Forwarding Heliotrope's alert. This looks like a multi-metric degradation (latency + 5xxs + throughput). I'm activating an "ops-cabinet" war-room for executive visibility. Goals: stabilize traffic, restore latency under 400ms p95 where possible, and provide customer-facing comms cadence.

Immediate asks:
- Kimberly: spin up a cross-region read-only reroute and validate model variant fallbacks (quantized v1?). Share config commands and expected failover time.
- Vanessa: pull live telemetry (GPU utilization, NVLink errors, queue depth, batching changes) and high-fidelity token traces for the last 90 minutes. Attach a CSV snapshot to the war-room notes.
- Grace: prepare a one-page exec summary and a customer-facing status note that I can send at :30 and again hourly.

I'll open a Zoom bridge at 09:18. Paging Laura for enablement with legal/CS if we need credits or SLA exceptions.

— Michael
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Bridge: zoom.us/j/834-xxx-xxxx (open)
PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-4472

Short update and actions taken (09:17):
- Rolled a model-variant failover for HELIO-42 to rwd-6b-v2-quantized (read replicas) — initial traffic ramp at 09:16.
- Applied temporary batching cap to reduce queue depth for long tail prompts.
- Throttled non-critical background jobs from HELIO-42 tenant via per-tenant rate limit override.

Preliminary observation: GPU queues were spiking on one shard (shard-3) and nvlink retransmits were elevated; suspect interconnect flakiness amplifying latency under high concurrency.

Requesting Vanessa's telemetry and the CSV snapshot for SLO analysis. Attaching a minimal SLO violations excerpt for quick review.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 11:03:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: ops-cabinet telemetry — Heliotrope (data snapshot attached)

Quick technical readout (11:03):
- Time window: 08:40–10:45 PDT
- Observed: sustained p95 token latency increase from 380ms -> 1.9s on shard-3 between 08:45–09:30; 5xx spike correlated with kernel retries and one node reporting elevated PCIe errors.
- GPU utilization: 72% avg but spikes to >98% on shard-3 during incidents — indicates hot spot rather than uniform load.
- Network: NVLink retransmit rate 6x baseline on affected node; host reported NIC interrupts which correlate to packet drops.
- Throughput: overall RPS down ~22% due to request timeouts and queue thrashing.

Mitigation applied (09:16–09:28):
- Failover to read-replicas on rwd-6b-v2-quantized (reduced per-token compute cost) — reduced p95 to ~520ms by 09:40 for routed traffic.
- Replaced offending node in the pool (node-3c) — hot swap completed at 10:12; NVLink errors subsided.
- Rebalanced traffic across shards and tightened batching cap.

Next steps:
- Full node post-mortem (Vanessa + infra) to confirm root cause (hardware vs. kernel regression).
- Provide customer-facing RCA and remediation timeline by EOD.

Attachment: performance_snapshot_0814.csv (stub)

— Vanessa
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Silva <j.silva@heliotropehealth.com>, ops@heliotropehealth.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Heliotrope production incident — initial customer update (12:05 PDT)

Jordan —

Short summary from Redwood's ops-cabinet:
- Symptom: latency and increased 5xxs affecting HELIO-42 production endpoints between ~08:45–10:12 PDT.
- Impact: intermittent timeouts for checkout flows; estimated 20–30% request degradation at peak.
- What we did: routed traffic to quantized read-replicas, throttled non-essential background traffic, and removed/replaced a problem node showing NVLink/PCIe errors.
- Current status: traffic restored to the primary fleet with p95 ~380–520ms for routed requests; error rate back to baseline for >90% of calls.

Planned follow-ups and timeline:
- EOD (by 17:00 PDT): consolidated RCA with remediation plan and mitigations to prevent recurrence.
- 48 hours: deployment of an interconnect firmware check and validation across similar nodes; if firmware is not the root cause we will schedule a controlled kernel rollback on affected image families.

We appreciate your patience and will keep this channel updated hourly until the RCA is delivered. If you'd like a deeper technical bridge, Vanessa and Kimberly are available now.

— Michael Grant
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
